references.text: The Israelites made a golden calf and declared that this was their god who brought them out of Egypt.
Moses recounts the Lord's words that the people had quickly turned away from the way the Lord had commanded them.
Moses reminds the people that they sinned by making a cast calf and quickly abandoned the way the Lord had commanded.
Israel quickly turned away from the way their fathers had walked and bowed down to other gods.
Jeroboam made two golden calves and told the people that these were their gods who brought them out of Egypt.
Nehemiah mentions that the fathers made a cast calf and said this was the god who brought them out of Egypt.
The psalmist describes how Israel made a calf at Horeb, worshiped a cast image, and exchanged their glory for an image of an ox.
Stephen tells how the Israelites made a calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the work of their hands.
Prophetic use of the golden calf as a symbol of man-made gods, directly linked to the event in the wilderness.
